title: The post-1969 band: Chick Corea material and Alan Broadbent's writing
summary: From 1969 on the band played composers like Corea, and Alan Broadbent's reworking of Blues in the Night was a triumph.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Why don't we talk a little bit about some of the key people in this band, because it was, like, people were saying, 'my gosh, it's like we haven't heard another one like this since the First Herd.' You remember, all the talk that was going on.
So it was heralding another era.
Yeah, but I think this has been a productive period from '69 on, as far as producing, once again, -- what I hope would be another approach and another way. We'd
gotten into the composer's music of this period, which is Chick Corea Correa and many others.

But I think that it's been a good period, because once again I wound up with some writing that's far and away the best of this period. I'm speaking now about people like Alan Broadbent and -- who I think did some phenomenal things. And being able to take an old piece of material, like Blues in the Night, and make it into something completely new and different, to me, that was a personal triumph for him and for me.
